name: Express.js Production REST API Track
description: Master Express.js web framework architecture, routing, middleware pipelines, error handling, JWT authentication, security best practices, and production REST API development.
whatYouLearn: Architect modular Express app routing structures
Write custom request processing middleware functions
Implement centralized global error handling middleware
Secure APIs using Helmet, CORS, and Rate Limiting
Handle file uploads using Multer multipart middleware
Build a production Blog Engine REST API

exercises.title: Express Application Setup & Basic Routing
exercises.description: Initialize an Express server app and handle GET/POST routes.
exercises.theory: Express simplifies Node.js HTTP server creation. Use app.get(), app.post(), and res.json() to handle route responses.
exercises.objective: Build an Express server with status and ping endpoints.
hints: app.use(express.json()) is required to automatically parse JSON request bodies into req.body

exercises.title: Route Parameters & Query Strings (req.params, req.query)
exercises.description: Extract dynamic URL parameters and search query strings.
exercises.theory: Route parameters (/users/:id) extract path variables into req.params. Query strings (?search=val) parse into req.query.
exercises.objective: Handle dynamic route parameters and query filters.
exercises.initialCode: // Handle /api/users/:userId route
hints: Colon prefix in route path (:userId) defines a named route parameter

exercises.title: Custom Application & Router Middleware
exercises.description: Write custom request logging and execution timing middleware functions.
exercises.theory: Express middleware functions receive (req, res, next). Call next() to pass control to the subsequent middleware function in stack.
exercises.objective: Build a custom request logger middleware.
requirements: Create middleware function taking (req, res, next)
Log request method, url, status code, and duration
hints: Always call next() inside custom middleware to avoid hanging requests

exercises.title: Modular Express Router Architecture (express.Router)
exercises.description: Modularize route endpoints across controller files using express.Router().
exercises.theory: express.Router() creates isolated, modular sub-routers that mount under specific path prefixes in the main app.
exercises.objective: Build and mount an isolated /api/v1/auth sub-router.
hints: Routes defined on sub-router are relative to its mounted parent path prefix
exercises.codeExample: const r = express.Router(); r.get('/list', fn); app.use('/api', r);

exercises.title: Global Error Handling Middleware
exercises.description: Centralize error responses using 4-parameter error handling middleware (err, req, res, next).
exercises.theory: Express identifies error-handling middleware by its 4-parameter signature (err, req, res, next). Pass errors to it using next(err).
exercises.objective: Build a global 4-parameter error handler middleware.
requirements: Define global error middleware with 4 parameters (err, req, res, next)
Return formatted JSON error payload with status code
Trigger handler by passing error to next(err)
hints: Error handling middleware must be registered AFTER all normal app routes
exercises.codeExample: app.use((err, req, res, next) => res.status(500).json({ err: err.message }));

exercises.title: JWT Authentication Middleware
exercises.description: Protect private API routes by verifying Bearer JWT Authorization headers.
exercises.theory: JWT authentication middleware inspects the Authorization header ('Bearer <token>'), verifies signature authenticity, and attaches user payload to req.user.
exercises.objective: Build a protect route middleware verifying Bearer tokens.
requirements: Attach user payload to req.user and call next()
hints: Return 401 Unauthorized when Authorization header is absent

exercises.title: API Security: Helmet & CORS Configuration
exercises.description: Secure Express HTTP headers using Helmet and configure CORS origins.
exercises.theory: Helmet sets security HTTP headers (X-Frame-Options, CSP, HSTS). CORS configures cross-origin browser access permissions.
exercises.objective: Configure CORS header simulation middleware.
requirements: Handle preflight OPTIONS request with 204 status
hints: Browsers send preflight OPTIONS requests before issuing POST/PUT cross-origin calls

exercises.title: Rate Limiting Middleware
exercises.description: Prevent DDoS and brute force attacks using client IP rate limiting.
exercises.theory: Rate limiting restricts the maximum number of requests a single client IP address can issue within a specified time window.
exercises.objective: Build an in-memory IP rate limiter middleware.
requirements: Track request hits per IP using Map
Return 429 Too Many Requests status when limit exceeded
Reset hit count after time window elapses
hints: HTTP status code 429 indicates client rate limit exceeded

exercises.title: Asynchronous Route Handler Wrapper (asyncHandler)
exercises.description: Eliminate repetitive try/catch blocks in async routes using an asyncHandler wrapper.
exercises.theory: asyncHandler wraps async express route functions to catch rejected promises automatically and forward them to next(err).
exercises.objective: Build a reusable asyncHandler utility wrapper.
requirements: Write higher-order asyncHandler function taking async route callback
hints: Promise.resolve(fn(req, res, next)).catch(next) forwards all uncaught errors to error middleware
exercises.codeExample: const asyncHandler = fn => (req, res, next) => Promise.resolve(fn(req, res, next)).catch(next);

exercises.title: Static File Serving (express.static)
exercises.description: Serve client assets, images, and HTML single-page apps using express.static.
exercises.theory: express.static middleware serves static assets (CSS, JS, images) directly from a specified public directory.
exercises.objective: Serve static assets from a public directory.
exercises.initialCode:
const path = require('path');
// Configure express.static
hints: Path prefix allows serving static assets from explicit URL routes

exercises.title: Cookie Parser & HTTP-Only Cookies
exercises.description: Set and read secure HTTP-Only cookies for session management.
exercises.theory: HTTP-Only cookies cannot be accessed by client-side JavaScript, protecting authentication session tokens against XSS attacks.
exercises.objective: Set secure HTTP-Only authentication cookie on login.
exercises.initialCode: // Set HTTP-Only cookie simulation
requirements: Set httpOnly: true, secure: true, and sameSite: 'strict'
hints: httpOnly: true prevents client-side document.cookie access

exercises.title: Request Input Validation Middleware (express-validator pattern)
exercises.description: Validate incoming HTTP request body fields before reaching route controllers.
exercises.theory: Validation middleware checks body field formatting (email syntax, password minimum length) and rejects invalid requests before controller execution.
exercises.objective: Build validation middleware checking email and password fields.
requirements: Check email format and password length
Return 400 Bad Request with errors array if invalid
hints: Returning 400 Bad Request prevents invalid requests from touching database logic

exercises.title: File Upload Multipart Middleware (Multer pattern)
exercises.description: Handle multipart/form-data file uploads and validate file extensions.
exercises.theory: File uploads require handling multipart/form-data request streams. Multipart middleware validates file MIME types and saves uploaded file buffers.
exercises.objective: Build single file upload validation middleware.
hints: Always validate file extensions and MIME types to prevent malicious script uploads

exercises.title: Express Sub-Applications & Mounting
exercises.description: Mount nested Express sub-applications for API versioning (/api/v1, /api/v2).
exercises.theory: Express allows mounting full sub-apps using app.use('/v1', v1SubApp) to manage versioned API releases cleanly.
exercises.objective: Mount v1 and v2 Express sub-apps under versioned route prefixes.
requirements: Create v1 and v2 sub-apps with express()
hints: API versioning isolates legacy endpoints while deploying modern schemas

exercises.title: HTTP Response Caching Headers (Cache-Control, ETag)
exercises.description: Configure client-side and CDN response caching headers.
exercises.theory: Cache-Control HTTP headers instruct browsers and CDNs how long response payloads can be cached before revalidation.
exercises.objective: Set Cache-Control and ETag headers for static data API endpoints.
requirements: Set ETag header for conditional request validation
hints: max-age=3600 specifies 1 hour client caching duration

exercises.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE) Push Stream Endpoints
exercises.description: Build real-time one-way push notification stream endpoints using Server-Sent Events.
exercises.theory: Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) keep HTTP connections open to push real-time updates from server to client.
exercises.objective: Build a SSE endpoint pushing periodic server updates.
requirements: Set Content-Type: text/event-stream and Connection: keep-alive headers
hints: SSE format requires double newline \n\n at the end of each message payload

exercises.title: Webhooks Receiver & Signature Verification
exercises.description: Receive and verify HMAC signatures on incoming external webhook callbacks.
exercises.theory: Webhooks receive HTTP POST notifications from external services. Verifying HMAC header signatures guarantees event payload authenticity.
exercises.objective: Verify incoming HMAC signature on a webhook endpoint.
requirements: Compute HMAC SHA-256 hash of JSON body
Return 401 Unauthorized if signatures do not match
hints: HMAC verification protects webhook endpoints against forged request payloads

exercises.title: Database Connection Pool Middleware Integration
exercises.description: Attach database connection handles to request objects via middleware.
exercises.theory: Attaching database pools to req.db via middleware simplifies dependency injection across route handlers.
exercises.objective: Build middleware binding mock database context to req.db.
requirements: Attach mockDb object to req.db inside middleware
hints: Attaching database handles to req objects simplifies unit testing
exercises.codeExample: app.use((req, res, next) => { req.db = db; next(); });

exercises.title: Graceful Server Shutdown & Socket Cleanup
exercises.description: Close server connections gracefully without dropping active HTTP requests.
exercises.theory: Graceful shutdown listens for termination signals, stops accepting new connections, and waits for pending requests to finish before exiting.
exercises.objective: Implement graceful server shutdown handler.
exercises.initialCode: // Implement server graceful shutdown
requirements: Include fallback timeout forcing process.exit(1) if connections hang
hints: Fallback timeouts prevent server shutdown hanging indefinitely if sockets remain open

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Production Blog Engine REST API
exercises.description: Build a production-grade Blog Engine REST API featuring Modular Routers, JWT Auth Middleware, Request Validation, Error Handlers, and Rate Limiting.
exercises.theory: This capstone project synthesizes Express.js architecture: express.Router modules, JWT authentication, request validation, rate limiting, and centralized 4-parameter error handling.
exercises.objective: Construct a complete Blog Engine REST API System.
exercises.initialCode: // Engineer complete Blog Engine REST API
requirements: Implement postsRouter with GET and POST /api/v1/posts
Protect creation endpoint with authGuard middleware
Add input validation and global error handling
hints: Combine express.Router() modularity with JWT auth guards and body validation

references.title: Express.js Official Guide
references.description: Comprehensive reference documentation for Express routing, middleware, and application APIs
